blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Supply chains can go wrong in many ways. A ship is delayed by weather. A supplier goes bankrupt. A border closes. A warehouse catches fire. A system fails at the worst moment.

Risk management is not about stopping all of this. It is about knowing which risks are likely, which risks matter most, and having a plan for the serious ones before they happen.

A small risk plan saves a large amount of damage. Prevention is cheaper than reaction. Good risk management does not remove risk — it reduces surprises.

items.q: What is the main idea of the text?
options: Risk management means planning for the serious risks
items.why: "having a plan for the serious ones before they happen" — a ideia central é planejar para os riscos sérios.

items.q: According to the text, what is risk management NOT about?
items.why: "Risk management is not about stopping all of this." Não é possível prevenir tudo.

items.q: The text says prevention is cheaper than reaction. This suggests that…
options: You should never react to problems
It is smart to plan before a problem happens
items.why: Inferência: se prevenir custa menos, planejar antes é a escolha inteligente.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Some risks matter more than others
A good plan removes all risk completely
A small plan can stop big damage
You should plan before problems happen
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que boa gestão "não remove o risco", só reduz surpresas.

items.q: Why does the text list a ship, a supplier, a border, a warehouse and a system?
options: To say weather is the biggest risk
To show these things are safe
To show that risks come from many places
items.why: Inferência: os exemplos mostram que os problemas vêm de fontes diferentes.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte apresentar os principais riscos ao novo diretor. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome to the team. Let me walk you through the top five risks on our register. These are the ones we watch every week.

Risk number one is supplier failure. If a key supplier goes bankrupt, the whole chain can stop. So for our main products we always keep a second supplier ready. If one fails, we call the other.

Risk number two is border delays. If a border closes, our ships wait, and we lose time and money. Number three is weather. If a storm hits the port, the ship is delayed. We cannot stop the weather, so we build extra days into the plan.

Number four is price. At Czarnikow, commodity prices move a lot. That risk never goes away, so we watch it every day. And number five is our systems. If a system fails at a busy time, we cannot see our stock.

None of these risks are new. The point is simple: we know which ones matter most, and we have a plan for each one. A small plan saves a large amount of damage.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is risk number one on Charlotte's list?
items.why: "Risk number one is supplier failure."

items.q: What does the team do about the supplier risk?
options: They keep a second supplier ready
items.why: "for our main products we always keep a second supplier ready."

items.q: Why does the team build extra days into the plan?
options: Because the border is always closed
Because they cannot stop the weather
items.why: "We cannot stop the weather, so we build extra days into the plan."

items.q: Charlotte says the price risk "never goes away." This suggests that…
options: The team can remove it with one plan
Price is not a real risk
The team must watch it all the time
The price will soon stop moving
items.why: Inferência: um risco que não some precisa de atenção contínua — por isso "we watch it every day".

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's message to the new director?
options: Calm and prepared — every risk has a plan
Worried that nothing can be done
items.why: Inferência: ela conhece os riscos e tem um plano para cada um — tom calmo e preparado.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The supplier went bankrupt, so it stopped all work." Bankrupt means…
items.why: Bankrupt = falido: sem dinheiro para pagar as contas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If a storm hits the port, the ship will ___ by two days."
items.why: To delay = atrasar; a tempestade faz o navio atrasar.

items.q: "We keep a backup plan to prevent big losses." To prevent means…
items.why: To prevent = prevenir, impedir que aconteça.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "This risk is very ___ , so we plan for it every week."
items.why: Likely = provável; um risco provável precisa de plano frequente. ("serious" cabe em sentido, mas o texto foca no que é frequente/provável para o plano semanal.)

items.q: "A good plan reduces the damage from a problem." Damage means…
items.why: Damage = dano: o prejuízo ou perda causado pelo problema.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em reuniões de risco. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The director must sign off on the risk plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new plan step by step." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar aos poucos, colocar em prática por etapas.

items.q: "If a risk is small, we do not need a backup plan." A backup plan is…
options: a second plan for when the first one fails
items.why: Backup plan = plano B, um segundo plano caso o primeiro falhe.

items.q: "The team agreed the plan but did not follow through." This means they…
options: did not finish what they agreed
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A small change will not move the needle on our risk." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, não faz diferença real.
